thread.title: Council applies for $702K in fed aid
thread.title_full: Council applies for $702K in fed aid

author: ohtadmin
title: Council applies for $702K in fed aid
text:
The town council has taken the next steps in trying to secure $702,000 in federal dollars to help improve the senior center and strengthen healthcare access.
Nearly 78% of that figure, $547,000, is being sought through the U.S. Department of Agriculture to improve the senior center, Town Administrator Ed Mello told the councilors Monday at their meeting. While he mentioned purchasing a generator for 6 West St. or upgrading the elevator — neither of which were included in the $1 million plan currently underway to renovate the building — nothing is set in stone.
“This would be for additional enhancements at the senior center,” he said. “We’re still working at refining what that is. But we don’t want to miss the opportunity. This is just the first step.”
The council approved a resolution that authorized the application to the USDA. The remaining $155,000 is being sought through the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services to participate in its Rural Health Transformation Program, which “empowers states to strengthen rural communities across America by improving healthcare access, quality and outcomes by transforming the healthcare delivery ecosystem. Through innovative system-wide change, the program invests in the rural healthcare delivery ecosystem for future generations.”
Jamestown was named one of 18 rural communities in Rhode Island eligible for the aid. The councilors authorized Mello to proceed with the application.
The money will be used to hire a consultant to undertake the first phase of planning. Mello said the contracted planner will work with stakeholders, including the fire department, schools and local doctors, to lay the foundation for a five-year strategic plan.
“Everybody has a seat at the table to discuss what the plan would look like,” he said. “This is not to fund the program. This is only to fund the development and planning of the program.”
Mello said the state is “anticipating the receipt of $156 million in funding” from Medicare to subsidize the program.
Gov. Dan McKee, who called it “a major win for Rhode Island,” announced the news in January.
“This funding allows us to strengthen the foundation of our healthcare system, improve outcomes and ensure Rhode Islanders can get the affordable, high-quality care they deserve,” he said.
The state’s director of health, Dr. Jerry Larkin, said the money will allow his department to “rethink how rural care is delivered.”
“I am looking forward to all the good that will come of this opportunity,” he said.
The key strategies include expanding access through federally qualified health centers, which are nonprofit clinics that provide comprehensive, affordable services to underserved communities, regardless of insurance.
McKee’s plan, moreover, expands access to hospital-level care in patients’ homes, which lowers costs and keeps families together during recovery.
